June Park: FYI looping in eng/infra + solutions — Infranova SI needs an architecture review and a short escalation plan. They hit a networking block on their private deploy tests. Can someone take a look? https://infranova.example.com/notes :eyes:

Alex Walker: I can take lead on the arch review. Quick ask: do we have the infra diagram + expected QPS/peak seq length? Also whether they want PrivateLink or site-to-site VPN.

Marcus (SI Solutions): Thanks — they said PrivateLink preferred but open to VPN if latency is an issue. Basic perf targets: 250 qps, p50 < 120ms, max seq 1024. I have their preliminary VPC diagram attached in the ticket (link above).

Lina Chen: Heads up on a few infra constraints: Private deployments require outbound access to our control plane on 443 (from a NATed IP range) and the serving nodes need to reach the model registry and S3 endpoint. Firewall rules they tried blocked 443 egress to our registry.

Alex Walker: Ok — for model sizing we need: model variant (fp16 vs int8), batch sizing, and whether KV cache persists across requests. If they're targeting 250 qps at p50 120ms we'll likely recommend a multi-GPU pool and quantized weights. Marcus, can you confirm model type?

Marcus (SI Solutions): They plan to serve a 7B decoder-only model (int8 quantized) with KV cache enabled. Batch target ~8. They've been running on a single node and seeing tail latency spikes.

Lina Chen: That aligns. Immediate checklist for them to unblock:
- allow outbound 443 to control-plane.redwood.ai (or our IP range)
- allow egress to model-registry.redwood.ai:443 and s3.region.amazonaws.com
- open inbound 1024-65535 ephemeral ports for inter-GPU comms if doing multi-node (or set up ENI-based placement)

Alex Walker: Also recommend these runtime flags on their private image to reduce latency spikes: `--batching=auto --max-batch-size=8 --kv-cache-enabled=true`

Marcus (SI Solutions): On the SI side I'll request infra changes and queue a firewall change today. Can we do a quick runbook for the fallback policy if PrivateLink fails? Suggested: route -> Dedicated pool (lower perf) then Hosted API as last resort.

Lina Chen: I can add the firewall snippet they can hand to their networking team:```
# allow egress to control plane & registry
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 34.200.1.5 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 52.17.77.10 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# ephemeral for cluster comms
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 1024:65535 -j ACCEPT
```

DeployBot: Scheduled: Arch review meeting set for Thu 11:00am PT — calendar invite sent to @June Park, @Alex Walker, @Marcus (SI Solutions), @Lina Chen.

June Park: Thanks everyone. Action items: Marcus to push firewall request today, Lina to validate control-plane IPs & add to runbook, Alex to prepare sizing recommendation (CPU/GPU per node + expected cost delta). We'll reconvene Thu 11. If anything blocks before then ping me directly. :thumbsup:
